programs.title: Storage Wars
programs.desc: The buyers trek to Murrieta, Calif.; Jeff Jarred resurfaces, but that doesn't sit well with the Dotsons; Barry Weiss figures a couple of things out; Jarrod and Brandi gamble on a unit and the results are electric.

programs.title: Rachael Ray's Meals in Minutes
programs.sub_title: Greek Meatballs and Spaghetti With Feta Sauce
programs.desc: Rachael goes on a Grecian adventure from her kitchen with a recipe for Greek-style lamb meatballs and her very own creation, feta-sghetti, a spaghetti dish served with a decadent white feta sauce.

programs.title: Rachael Ray's Meals in Minutes
programs.sub_title: Lucca Style Pesto Pasta or Trenette Al Pesto
programs.desc: Rachael prepares a classic pesto sauce using fresh basil, roasted pistachios and pine nuts, combined with Pecorino and Parmigiano cheeses; she then cooks it Lucca style with potatoes and green beans and serves it over large pasta.

programs.title: Rachael Ray's Meals in Minutes
programs.sub_title: Loaded Street Corn Nachos and Carne Asada Salad
programs.desc: Rachael shows how to bring the festive spirit of Cinco de Mayo to any day with her indulgent street corn nachos loaded with Mexican crema. She also whips up a vibrant carne asada salad featuring sautéed skirt steak, a fresh mix of lettuce, and a zesty avocado dressing. To keep the celebration going, John shakes up a tequila-based cocktail he calls the Margarita Piña Colada.

programs.title: Rachael Ray's Meals in Minutes
programs.sub_title: Harissa & Fire-Roasted Tomato Spaghetti with Speck and Toasted Almonds
programs.desc: Speck, a smoked prosciutto coated in black pepper, is one of Rachael's favorite ingredients, and she puts it to good use in her original recipe for Harissa and Fire-Roasted Tomato Spaghetti. The bold pasta dish is finished with toasted almonds and served alongside charred artichokes. To complement the meal, John mixes up two playful adult fountain drinks made with fresh cherries and vodka.

programs.title: The Chef's Garden
programs.desc: Native Clevelander, chef, and restaurateur Douglas Katz visits The Chef's Garden to meet with Farmer Lee Jones and explore the world of early season tomatoes; passionate about global cuisines, Chef Katz delves into how different cultures use tomatoes in diverse ways throughout a dish; after sampling a variety of early tomatoes, they return to the Culinary Vegetable Institute, where Chef Katz creates an Indian-inspired tomato and lentil dish.
